# [CS060] Dependency Violates Module Policy (dependency-policy-denied)

A module matches denied_prefixes or falls outside allowed_prefixes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Supply Chain & Provenance |
| **CWE** | [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html) |
| **OWASP** | A03:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

dependencies.denied_prefixes blocks modules and organizations, and a non-empty allowed_prefixes allows only the listed ones, for direct and indirect requirements alike.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```text
# codex.yaml
dependencies:
  denied_prefixes: [github.com/dgrijalva]
# go.mod
require github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go v3.2.0+incompatible
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```text
require github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 v5.2.1
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [dependency-policy-denied]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    dependency-policy-denied: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore dependency-policy-denied -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** dependency-policy-denied
```
